To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a process management approach can foster meaningful collaboration between partners in public–private partnership projects.

a process management approach can be used to design public–private partnership agreements that are structured to deepen the cooperation between the partners and deliver project outcomes better than either partner could achieve on its own.
public–private partnerships can create value for both partners by fostering meaningful partnerships.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the structure of a partnership, the process of managing a partnership, and the outcomes that a partnership can produce can be enhanced through innovative partnership design.
the design of public–private partnerships that can create value for all partners and the public at large.
the design of innovative public–private partnerships and the management of these partnerships through a process management orientation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
public–private partnerships can be designed to foster meaningful cooperation, and that process management can play a central role in achieving this objective.
the process management approach to partnership can create value for all parties by fostering meaningful partnerships that can deliver projects that benefit society.

public–private partnerships can deliver more value to the public when the partnership is structured to be more like a collaboration than a contract, and when the process management orientation to the partnership is used to build trust, share risks and foster public support for the partnership.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a process management perspective on partnership is an effective means of fostering meaningful public–private partnerships.
public–private partnerships can be structured and managed to deliver meaningful collaboration and create value for all partners.

a partnership process management orientation to public–private partnerships can help create value by deepening cooperation between the public and private partners, and delivering project outcomes that are more valuable than what either partner would be able to deliver on their own.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of a partnership should be guided by the need to create value for all partners and the public, not just by the need to reduce risk.

public–private partnerships are more than simply a procurement model, and that the design of a partnership should be based on an understanding of how to build trust, share risks, and foster public support.
public–private partnerships can be structured to create value for all stakeholders, and the process management approach to partnership can be an important tool to achieve that goal.
